subject: Intermittent app errors and token latency — suspected egress inspection / peering path
messages:
From: Sam Cole <sam.cole@cloudpath.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@cloudpath.com; maria.lopez@cloudpath.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: High error rate and slow token times to Redwood endpoints

Hannah —

We're seeing elevated 5xx rates and tokenization spikes when our app talks to your hosted inference endpoints (us-west-2). This started around 07:40 PST and is intermittent but persistent. Throughput looks normal but tail latency for generation requests jumps into multiple seconds and occasionally returns 502/503. Our customers are reporting feature outages.

We opened this with our infra team and captured a HAR/trace (attached). Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (routing, peering) this morning?

Sam
Sam Cole
CloudPath Solutions — Head of Platform Partnerships

Attachments: rp-trace-20270210.har

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Cole <sam.cole@cloudpath.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High error rate and slow token times to Redwood endpoints

Sam — thanks for the trace. I'm escalating to infra immediately. A few quick asks while we triage:
- Can you confirm the affected routes (source subnets / egress IPs) and whether this is only via your peered VPC or from multiple networks?
- Can you reproduce with a simple curl command? If so, include timestamped response headers.

I'll loop in our SREs now. Apologies for the interruption — we'll prioritize.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Enterprise Success | Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: RE: High error rate and slow token times to Redwood endpoints

Hannah / team — I dug into infra metrics for us-west-2:
- Host-level CPU/GPU utilization is nominal.
- Ingress requests to API gateway show increased 504/502 at ~07:38–08:05 but origin (serving runtime) responded normally for most traces we have.
- However, we see spikes in TCP handshake and SYN retransmits from a small set of CloudPath egress IPs.

Initial hypothesis: something on the egress path (CloudPath side, or an intermediate firewall/inspection appliance) is causing packet drops or head-of-line delays. Could be deep packet inspection (DPI) or an upstream peering flap.

I've started a packet capture request with engineering and asked ops to correlate with BGP session flaps.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cloudpath.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@cloudpath.com; sam.cole@cloudpath.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High error rate and slow token times to Redwood endpoints

Rishi — thanks for the quick look. We confirmed the problematic source addresses are our egress NAT pool (52.23.14.0/27). We also saw a spike in our perimeter firewall CPU and an increase in TLS inspection re-handshakes. We rolled a rule change at 08:50 (temporary bypass for traffic to redwood-inference.example.net) which reduced error rate for a short time, but the problem recurred when traffic hit a different inspection cluster.

We believe this may be a pooling/load-balancing issue in their inspection layer that intermittently routes flows through overloaded workers. We're happy to keep collaborating on mitigations — next step from our side is to request provider escalation and provide full capture (attached: egress-dpi-sample.txt).

— Maria
Maria Lopez
Head of SRE, CloudPath Solutions

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: High error rate and slow token times — exec and mitigations

Folks — forwarding the customer thread. Maria requested provider escalation. Sam is asking for an exec-level summary. Please prepare a short mitigation plan and an outreach draft for the cloud provider + CloudPath. Key points to include:
- Temporary traffic steering options (route CloudPath to a fallback peering / alternate egress region)
- Option to provision dedicated ingress pool for CloudPath (short-term reserved instances)
- Ask CloudPath to request their firewall vendor to pin flows or disable DPI for our endpoints while we validate.

I want a summary for the VP by EOD. — Hannah

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: High error rate and slow token times — exec and mitigations

Summary for exec / runbook (draft):
1) Impact: CloudPath reports intermittent 5xx and increased generation tail latency for ~2k TPS peak client requests; user-facing errors for several customers.
2) Short-term mitigations (1–4 hrs):
   - Route CloudPath traffic to our us-east-1 fallback peering endpoint (we can add a DNS CNAME redirect / short TTL).
   - Bypass DPI by adding explicit allow-list for CloudPath egress IPs on their perimeter (customer action) and request provider to pin connections.
   - Increase gateway capacity + reduce per-connection inspection timeouts; enable connection pooling and longer idle timeouts to keep KV caches warm.
3) Medium-term (24–72 hrs):
   - Provision a dedicated ingress pool for CloudPath (reserved capacity on dedicated infra) to isolate from inspection-induced variance.
   - Audit BGP/peering paths with provider and CloudPath; adjust BGP communities to prefer lower-latency path.
4) Ask for visibility: full pcap, TLS handshake timings, and firewall logs (CloudPath to provide).

I'll draft the outreach note for provider escalation. If approved, Hannah please send to CloudPath exec and cc VP Sales.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Platform Reliability

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: sam.cole@cloudpath.com; maria.lopez@cloudpath.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai; priyom_das@redwood.ai; olga_petrov@redwood.ai; vp-sales@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 19:34:00 -0800
Subject: Exec summary and immediate plan — CloudPath latency & errors (RDW-3942)

Sam / Maria —

Thank you again for the quick escalation. Below is our agreed immediate plan and what we are doing on our side.

Executive summary (for customers / execs):
- Problem: Intermittent high tail latency and 502/503 responses affecting a subset of CloudPath traffic between their egress NAT pool and our us-west-2 ingress. Root cause appears to be intermittent overload and flow rebalancing in an intermediate DPI/firewall inspection cluster on CloudPath's egress path.
- Action taken (completed): Rishi correlated SYN retransmits to CloudPath egress IPs and we validated origin service health; Maria confirmed temporary firewall rule changes reduced errors briefly.
- Immediate mitigations (in flight):
  1) DNS steering: We created a us-east-1 fallback CNAME (short TTL 60s) and will update routing for CloudPath egress IP ranges to the fallback peering. This should reduce error exposure while provider escalates inspection cluster.
  2) Dedicated ingress: We approved reserving 2x dedicated gateway instances for CloudPath for 72 hours to reduce shared-path variance; provisioning ETA 90 minutes.
  3) Provider escalation: CloudPath will open an expedited ticket with their firewall vendor and provider; we provided packet captures and logs (attached).

What we need from CloudPath now:
- Full firewall logs and provider ticket id (so we can coordinate).
- Confirm whether they can temporarily pin flows or disable DPI for redwood-inference.example.net.

Next update: I will share status in 1 hour and again when the fallback routing is live. If you want an executive call, please propose a time.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Enterprise Success | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0192
